title: Sprint 6j: a server prepared with no project, its own VPN, project admins admitted, locked and purged, a project registered and taken off

steps.say:
0-1. What this walk needs, all on the laptop in your own account. It rents one server at Scaleway for about 60 minutes and gives it back at the end.

- keepassxc-cli: sudo apt install keepassxc-minimal (once, in a separate terminal).
- Your Scaleway key, set in Forges (or kept with porelo-host key set scaleway), and your Scaleway project UUID from Scaleway Console -> Project -> Settings.
- Your secrets file ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx with its master password (walk 18).
- porelo-host's guide for the host steps beside you: doc/guides/6j-host.md of porelo-host, steps host-prepare, host-person-admit, host-person-lock, host-person-purge, host-project-register, and host-project-remove, together with the 6j test collection tarball (.tar.gz) and its 64-digit SHA-256 built there for this development build's test collection step.
- A second person's public key block for the admit step, one line <laptop> <ssh-ed25519 …> <WireGuard public key>, and a project signing public key as one ssh-ed25519 … line with no comment. Make them in a terminal on the laptop:

  ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N '' -f /tmp/walk-admin
  wg genkey | tee /tmp/walk-admin.wg | wg pubkey

  Print the exact one-line key block to paste in step 3-2 (walklaptop ssh-ed25519 <base64> <WireGuard-public-key>, one space between fields, no comment):

  printf 'walklaptop %s %s\n' "$(awk '{print $1, $2}' /tmp/walk-admin.pub)" "$(wg pubkey < /tmp/walk-admin.wg)"

  Print the exact project signing key line to paste in step 4-2 (ssh-ed25519 <base64>, no comment):

  awk '{print $1, $2}' /tmp/walk-admin.pub

Start the interface from ~/git/porelo-frontend with --roles host-admin (it builds porelo-host from this checkout into ~/.porelo/walk/porelo-host, builds the Linux debug bundle, and starts the bundle directly rather than through flutter run so snap confinement does not block wg-quick):

mkdir -p ~/.porelo/walk && cp doc/walks/22-sprint-6j-a-server-prepared-with-no-project.json ~/.porelo/walk/walk.json && (cd packages/porelo_host && dart compile exe bin/porelo_host.dart -o ~/.porelo/walk/porelo-host) && flutter build linux --debug && PORELO_HOST_STANDIN=$HOME/.porelo/walk/porelo-host PORELO_WALK=$HOME/.porelo/walk build/linux/x64/debug/bundle/porelo_frontend --roles host-admin

This panel moves on by itself when it sees what a step waits for; where you are ahead of it, click Next in this panel. Once all of this is in place, click Next here.

1-1. On the laptop, in the interface: open Find a command in the title bar (press Ctrl+K or click the search icon beside Watch another machine…) and click Prepare a server… in the Machines group. Expected: the wizard Prepare a server opens at Step 1 of 7 — Where it is rented, showing Scaleway project id and Set Scaleway key, with no Account on the server field. Failure signs: Prepare a server… is absent from the finder (--roles host-admin was omitted at startup) or marked unavailable (keepassxc-cli is missing).

1-2. On the laptop, in the interface (Step 1 of 7 — Where it is rented): type your Scaleway project UUID into Scaleway project id (if your Scaleway key is not stored yet, click Set Scaleway key first and enter it in its terminal), then click Next. Expected (not run): the Scaleway key check succeeds and Step 2 of 7 — Your server opens, proposing the lowest unused network number <n> (such as 0) with Run a forge on this server turned on; no project step is shown. Failure signs: Copy the project id from Scaleway Project, Settings. below Next, or a Scaleway key error keeping the wizard on Step 1.

1-3. On the laptop, in the interface (Step 2 of 7 — Your server): type walk6j into Server name, keep the proposed integer <n> in Network number (0–255) (note <n> for the 10.73.<n>.0/24 and porelo-<n> checks below), leave Run a forge on this server turned on, and click Next. Expected: Step 3 of 7 — Your ssh keys opens. Failure signs: Next stays disabled with This laptop already knows a host with that name or network. Choose another. or The server name needs one DNS label….

1-4. On the laptop, in the interface (Step 3 of 7 — Your ssh keys): enter your rental SSH private key path (such as ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) in Your private ssh key, confirm Your public ssh key holds the matching .pub path with a check mark, and click Next. Expected: Step 4 of 7 — Your secrets file opens with ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx in Your secrets file (.kdbx), It is there: setup opens it with its master password., and Open it now. Failure signs: a refusal on Your public ssh key saying the pair does not match, or a missing key file keeping Next disabled.

1-5. On the laptop, in the interface (Step 4 of 7 — Your secrets file): confirm ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx is in Your secrets file (.kdbx), click Open it now, type the master password of ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx into the terminal and press Enter, then click Done. Expected (not run): nothing you type is shown; keepassxc-cli records hosts/walk6j/wireguard in ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx and the terminal prints The secrets file is ready.; after Done, the step shows Ready: the file keeps the server’s keys. Failure signs: did not open with that password; type it again., or The secrets file was not opened, so setup did not start.

1-6. On the laptop, in the interface (Step 4 to Step 5 of 7 — A test collection, shown in a development build): click Next, enter the 6j test collection .tar.gz path in Test collection (.tar.gz) and its 64-digit hex digest in Test collection SHA-256, then click Next. Expected: Step 6 of 7 — Check and start opens with the summary Scaleway project id: …, Server: walk6j, Network: 10.73.<n>.0/24, Forge: on, No project or project account is created., your SSH keys, Secrets file: ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx, and the test collection, plus the button Prepare the server. Failure signs: Give the test collection SHA-256 as 64 hexadecimal digits. or The test collection does not exist….

1-7. On the laptop, in the interface (Step 6 of 7 — Check and start): verify every line of the summary, then click Prepare the server — from here on a server is rented — and when Step 7 of 7 — Preparing the server pauses at its stop, click Complete setup on the host. Expected (not run): porelo-host up runs with --host-name walk6j --network <n> --login-user root --forge true and no project bundle or project account, then pauses waiting for you; Complete setup on walk6j opens asking only for the host's VPN key and its forge's certificate from your secrets file (no vault passphrase, no vault entries, no Tresorit login, no Matrix token). Failure signs: a refused step in the protocol, or Complete setup on walk6j asking for any secret other than wireguard and forge-certificate.

1-8. On the laptop, in the interface (Complete setup on walk6j): click Open the terminal, type only the master password of ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx once into the terminal and press Enter (nothing else is asked), then click Done. Expected (not run): nothing you type is shown; a lasting CA for walk6j is stored in ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx under hosts/walk6j/forge-ca-key and hosts/walk6j/forge-ca (constrained to walk6j.porelo.internal and 10.73.<n>.0/24), certificates for forge.walk6j.porelo.internal and matrix.walk6j.porelo.internal are signed locally, wireguard and forge-certificate are piped to porelo-host-stop --stdin, and the terminal says The host has what it needs; setup goes on.; Done closes the stop dialog and resumes up. Failure signs: has no entry hosts/walk6j/wireguard; nothing was sent., The host's certificates could not be signed; nothing was sent., or Host setup ended with code 64: a wrong call.

1-9. On the laptop, in the interface, then on the host via porelo-host's guide: wait for up to end ready (up checked in the protocol, and For the project admins shown below it). When Bring the VPN up for walk6j opens by itself, click Cancel it twice and click Finish so step 2-1 brings the VPN up from walk6j's row in Machines (if you already typed your sudo password there, click Finish and go on). Now work through doc/guides/6j-host.md of porelo-host, step host-prepare, against the server (such as 192.0.2.10), then come back here and click Next in this panel. Expected (not run): up ends ready with host.json checked, and every host-prepare check on the server passes (/etc/porelo-host/host.json, WireGuard, Forgejo, homeserver, and no project or project user created). Failure signs: host.json is missing from the completed server setup. or a host.json mismatch in the protocol, or any check failing in host-prepare.

2-1. On the laptop, in the interface: in the rail click Machines. Click walk6j's row and click Bring the VPN up — or, if walk6j already shows as Prepared, click its chevron (Show more), open its menu (⋮), run Take the VPN down with your sudo password, then open its menu (⋮) again and click Bring the VPN up to exercise the machine row's VPN command. Type only your sudo password into Bring the VPN up for walk6j and press Enter, verify the tunnel on the laptop, then click Next in this panel. Expected (not run): the terminal installs porelo-<n>, confirms a fresh WireGuard handshake, trusts walk6j's CA and writes forge.walk6j.porelo.internal and matrix.walk6j.porelo.internal into /etc/hosts, then closes; walk6j stands in Machines as Prepared; in a separate terminal on the laptop, ip -br addr show porelo-<n> shows 10.73.<n>.2/32 and ping -c 1 10.73.<n>.1 answers. Failure signs: The VPN check did not confirm this server., The VPN command cannot run (snap confinement or an existing porelo-<n> collision), walk6j staying in preparation, or 10.73.<n>.1 not answering.

2-2. On the laptop, in the interface: on walk6j's row in Machines, click its chevron (Show more) if closed, open its menu (⋮) (or machine-menu on walk6j's own page), and click For the project admins…. Expected (not run): the dialog For the project admins opens. Failure signs: For the project admins… is unavailable (complete the server setup first) or missing (--roles host-admin omitted).

2-3. On the laptop, in the interface (For the project admins): inspect all eight public values — address, endpoint (<address>:51820), wireguard_public_key, network (10.73.<n>.0/24), ssh_host_key, ca_sha256, homeserver (matrix.walk6j.porelo.internal), and SSH fingerprint (SHA256:…) — click each or any copy button (such as Copy address) to verify copying to the clipboard, then click Close. Expected (not run): all eight values match /etc/porelo-host/host.json on the server, each has its own working copy button, and Close dismisses the dialog. Failure signs: any of the eight rows missing, a value differing from /etc/porelo-host/host.json, or a copy button leaving the clipboard empty.

3-1. On the laptop, in the interface: open walk6j's menu (⋮) and click Admit a project admin…. In Step 1 of 4 — Project admin account, type walkadmin and click Next. Expected: the wizard Admit a project admin opens and advances to Step 2 of 4 — Laptop public keys. Failure signs: Next stays disabled with Use a name starting with a lower-case letter….

3-2. On the laptop, in the interface (Step 2 of 4 — Laptop public keys): paste the one-line key block from step 0-1 (walklaptop ssh-ed25519 <base64> <WireGuard-public-key>, one space between fields, no comment) into Laptop public keys, click Next, check the summary on Step 3 of 4 — Check and start, and click Admit a project admin. Expected (not run): /usr/local/sbin/porelo-host-person add walkadmin --role project-admin runs over root SSH with the key block on standard input, and Step 4 of 4 shows walkadmin is admitted as a project admin. followed by walklaptop: 10.73.<n>.3. Failure signs: Line 1: … refusing a key comment or extra spaces before Next, or a verbatim porelo-host-person: … refusal on Step 4.

3-3. On the laptop, in the interface, then on the host via porelo-host's guide: click Finish to close Admit a project admin, work through doc/guides/6j-host.md of porelo-host, step host-person-admit, on the server, then come back here and click Next in this panel. Expected (not run): the dialog closes; on the server, host-person-admit confirms walkadmin's OS account, SSH key, WireGuard peer 10.73.<n>.3/32, Forgejo account, and for Matrix the token file listed on the server (not run, where porelo-host's guide marks that check not run). Failure signs: walkadmin's account, WireGuard peer, Forgejo user, or Matrix token file missing on the server.

4-1. On the laptop, in the interface: open walk6j's menu (⋮) and click Register a project…. In Step 1 of 5 — Project name, type walk6j-demo and click Next; in Step 2 of 5 — Project admin account, type walkadmin and click Next. Expected: the wizard Register a project advances to Step 3 of 5 — Project signing public key. Failure signs: Next stays disabled with Use a name starting with a lower-case letter….

4-2. On the laptop, in the interface (Step 3 of 5 — Project signing public key): paste the project's signing key line from step 0-1 (ssh-ed25519 <base64>, with no comment) into Project signing public key, click Next, check the summary on Step 4 of 5 — Check and start, and click Register a project. Expected (not run): /usr/local/sbin/porelo-host-project add walk6j-demo walkadmin --signed-by 'ssh-ed25519 …' runs over root SSH, and Step 5 of 5 shows Project walk6j-demo is registered for walkadmin. Organization: <organization>. Publisher: porelo-publisher-walk6j-demo. Failure signs: Give one ssh-ed25519 public key with no comment. before Next, or a verbatim porelo-host-project: … refusal on Step 5.

4-3. On the laptop, in the interface, then on the host via porelo-host's guide: click Finish to close Register a project, work through doc/guides/6j-host.md of porelo-host, step host-project-register, on the server, then come back here and click Next in this panel. Expected (not run): the dialog closes; on the server, host-project-register confirms the organization for walk6j-demo, walkadmin's membership, the publisher account porelo-publisher-walk6j-demo, and the pinned signing key. Failure signs: the organization, porelo-publisher-walk6j-demo, or project record missing on the server.

5-1. On the laptop, in the interface: open walk6j's menu (⋮) and click Take the project off. In Step 1 of 3 — Project name, type walk6j-demo and click Next, then on Step 2 of 3 — Check and start click Take the project off. Expected (not run): the terminal Take walk6j-demo off the server opens inside the interface, asking for the master password of ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx. Failure signs: Take the project off is unavailable (no secrets file was kept from server preparation), or keepassxc-cli is missing.

5-2. On the laptop, in the interface (Take walk6j-demo off the server): type the master password of ~/Porelo/secrets.kdbx into the terminal and press Enter, then click Done once the helper finishes. Expected (not run): nothing you type is shown; even if shared/forge-central-token is absent (the terminal prints has no entry shared/forge-central-token; nothing was sent.), removal succeeds because walk6j-demo has no repository in 6j and needs no central token; the helper answers {"project":"walk6j-demo","removed":true}, the terminal prints The helper has answered. Close this terminal to read its answer., and after Done, Step 3 of 3 shows The project walk6j-demo was taken off the server. Failure signs: did not open with that password three times, The terminal was closed before the host confirmed project removal., or a verbatim porelo-host-project: … refusal on Step 3.

5-3. On the laptop, in the interface, then on the host via porelo-host's guide: click Finish to close Take the project off, work through doc/guides/6j-host.md of porelo-host, step host-project-remove, on the server, then come back here and click Next in this panel. Expected (not run): the dialog closes; on the server, host-project-remove confirms walk6j-demo's organization, porelo-publisher-walk6j-demo, and project state are gone. Failure signs: walk6j-demo or porelo-publisher-walk6j-demo still present on the server.

6-1. On the laptop, in the interface: open walk6j's menu (⋮) and click Lock. In Step 1 of 3 — Project admin account, type walkadmin, click Next, and on Step 2 of 3 — Check and start click Lock a project admin. Expected (not run): /usr/local/sbin/porelo-host-person lock walkadmin runs over root SSH, answers {"person":"walkadmin","locked":true}, and Step 3 of 3 shows walkadmin is locked. Failure signs: a verbatim porelo-host-person: … refusal or The host helper could not be reached: … on Step 3.

6-2. On the laptop, in the interface, then on the host via porelo-host's guide: click Finish to close Lock a project admin, work through doc/guides/6j-host.md of porelo-host, step host-person-lock, on the server, then come back here and click Next in this panel. Expected (not run): the dialog closes; on the server, host-person-lock confirms walkadmin's SSH, WireGuard peer, and service access are disabled while walkadmin's records remain. Failure signs: walkadmin's SSH login or WireGuard peer still active on the server.

7-1. On the laptop, in the interface: open walk6j's menu (⋮) and click Purge. In Step 1 of 3 — Project admin account, type walkadmin, click Next, on Step 2 of 3 — Check and start click Purge a project admin, and in the second-decision prompt Purge walkadmin after locking? click Purge permanently. Expected (not run): nothing runs until Purge permanently is clicked; then /usr/local/sbin/porelo-host-person purge walkadmin runs over root SSH, answers {"person":"walkadmin","purged":true}, and Step 3 of 3 shows walkadmin is purged. Failure signs: purge running without the Purge walkadmin after locking? prompt, or a verbatim porelo-host-person: … refusal on Step 3.

7-2. On the laptop, in the interface, then on the host via porelo-host's guide: click Finish to close Purge a project admin, work through doc/guides/6j-host.md of porelo-host, step host-person-purge, on the server, then come back here and click Next in this panel. Expected (not run): the dialog closes; on the server, host-person-purge confirms walkadmin and walklaptop are permanently removed from the server's state, accounts, and WireGuard peers. Failure signs: any account, state file, or WireGuard peer for walkadmin remaining on the server.

8-1. On the laptop, in the interface: open walk6j's menu (⋮) and click Give the server back, click Give the server back in Take the server for walk6j down?, type only your sudo password into Take the VPN down for walk6j and press Enter, click Done when it ends, then click Close. Expected (not run): porelo-host down confirms give-back at Scaleway, the VPN terminal removes porelo-<n> together with walk6j's /etc/hosts lines and trusted CA, the dialog shows Done., walk6j leaves Machines, and in a separate terminal on the laptop ip link show porelo-<n> reports that porelo-<n> does not exist (and if you made /tmp/walk-admin* in 0-1, rm -f /tmp/walk-admin /tmp/walk-admin.pub /tmp/walk-admin.wg cleans them up). Failure signs: The server give-back was not confirmed. Recovery has been kept., The server is given back; the VPN on this computer is still up, walk6j still listed in Machines or the Scaleway console, or porelo-<n> still present. Then tell me what differed.
